findings.title: Remembering as maintenance against deformation
findings.claim: The command to remember can operate as active preservation of the covenantal and semantic integrity of the gifts being recalled, because the nearby sequence shows breach, hardening, displacement, and forgetting as ways a bestowed order unravels.
findings.mechanism: The focus imperative to remember is placed against the supplied sequence of covenant undoing, hardened hearts, displaced words, and forgotten portions. That contact changes recollection from a flattering look backward into upkeep that resists social and semantic deformation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive remembrance as work that keeps an entrusted order intact, not only as retrieval of a past event.
findings.containment: The ordinary command remains a collective call to remember Allah's favor. This qualified contextual reading adds a maintenance frame and does not claim that the focus itself narrates a completed deformation.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and pericope anchor coordinates agree, but the support is a legacy-unbound HFT nomination; the inference is therefore retained as qualified and attributed.

findings.title: Prophets as repair after a gap
findings.claim: The prophets placed among the people can be read as recurring repair points that restore intelligibility and a navigable route after concealment or interruption.
findings.mechanism: The focus names prophets within the addressed community; the supplied context pairs clarification with light, guidance with a path, and a messenger with an interval from messengers. Their contact changes prophetic presence from ancestral prestige into a repair function that reopens disclosure and direction.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why prophetic presence matters in this local sequence: it restores a route when transmission has dimmed or paused.
findings.containment: The ordinary claim that prophets were placed among the people remains intact. This is a qualified function-level reading, not a claim that the focus names a permanent social mechanism beyond the supplied pericope.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and pericope anchor coordinates agree, but the support is a legacy-unbound HFT nomination and the target context lacks morphology; the inference is retained as qualified and attributed.

findings.title: Kingship within a delegated domain
findings.claim: Being made kings grants a real sphere of public disposal whose source, limit, and accountability remain within God's encompassing dominion.
findings.mechanism: The focus names the people as kings after the supplied context denies effective possession against God, assigns dominion over the heavens and earth to God twice, and names divine creation. The repeated ownership frame changes royal status from self-standing sovereignty into delegated authority.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold human kingship as genuine agency and derivative agency at the same time.
findings.containment: The ordinary historical status of kingship remains present. The contextual reading adds a nested source and limit; it does not collapse human public authority into divine sovereignty.

epistemic.reason: The focus and context ownership coordinates agree, but the support is a legacy-unbound HFT nomination; the nested-delegation inference is retained as qualified and attributed.
